summary:
We developed Earth Jukebox, an interactive web application that transforms visual data into music through real-time data sonification. Built with HTML5, CSS3, and pure JavaScript using the Web Audio API, the tool scans images pixel by pixel, mapping brightness levels to musical notes and RGB color dominance to distinct synthesizer waveforms. Users can explore built-in Earth science visualizations—such as thermal anomalies, ocean currents, and atmospheric aerosols—or upload any personal image to hear it come alive.
Earth Jukebox addresses the challenge of making complex scientific and environmental data intuitive and accessible. Relying solely on visual charts can be overwhelming and excludes people with visual impairments. By translating visual contrasts into harmonic scales, anyone can perceive temperature shifts and hidden patterns simply by listening.
This project is important because it unites science, art, and inclusion. It empowers visually impaired individuals to experience images and maps through sound, offers a creative way to monitor our planet's changing climate, and lays the groundwork for hearing invisible cosmic data from space telescopes as a universal symphony.
